title: Relative first cohomology and torsors with a specified open section
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme, $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ a closed immersion, and $j:V=T\setminus Z\hookrightarrow T$ its open complement. Let $G$ be an abelian sheaf on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Use the derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. A $G$-torsor [def-sc-gm-torsor] means a sheaf of sets with a $G$-action which is locally equivariantly isomorphic to $G$ acting on itself. Use derived global sections $R\Gamma$ and their cohomology as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], and the mapping cone and shift of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put
$$H^q(T,V;G)=H^q\bigl(\operatorname{Cone}(R\Gamma(T,G)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(V,j^{-1}G))[-1]\bigr).$$
There is a canonical bijection between $H^1(T,V;G)$ and the isomorphism classes of pairs $(P,s)$ consisting of a $G$-torsor $P$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ and a section $s\in(j^{-1}P)(V)$; isomorphisms must carry the specified section to the specified section. It sends the trivial torsor with its identity section to zero. The map $H^1(T,V;G)\to H^1(T,G)$ forgets $s$ and gives the ordinary torsor class. This bijection is natural under morphisms $G\to G'$ (contracted product of torsors [def-sc-contracted-product-presentation]) and under morphisms of schemes $h:T'\to T$, with $V'=h^{-1}V$, followed by any coefficient morphism $h^{-1}G\to G'$.
For any short exact sequence $0\to G_1\to G_2\to G_3\to0$, the relative groups have the natural connecting maps $H^q(T,V;G_3)\to H^{q+1}(T,V;G_1)$; these commute with forgetting the specified support and with the preceding pullback and coefficient maps.
